title: The normalized integral Hom reduction presentations give the same morphism
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite field extension, and $X$ a scheme. Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with $\ell\ne D.p$, solely for the legacy coefficient interface. For $n\ge0$, use the completed integral coefficient sheaf and its positive quotient of exponent $n+1$. Let $a$ be any normalized TensorPresentation and $m$ any ReductionPresentation of $a$ at $n$ [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models]. For all ordinary unbounded derived inputs $K,L$, the canonical morphism integralHomReductionComparison [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-comparison] equals IntegralHom.comparison defined by $m$, as a morphism from reduction of the recorded ambient Hom to Hom of the two reductions. This asserts equality of the evaluation-transpose maps themselves, not merely isomorphic endpoints.

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the inverse target adjunction Hom equivalence. The split representative normalization theorem identifies the uncurried canonical comparison with the normalized map prescribed by m; unfolding IntegralHom.comparison identifies the latter with the uncurried form of m.comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem integralHomComparison_normalization
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{d}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ)
    (a : IntegralHom.TensorPresentation.{u, u} X
      (completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E X D hl))
    (m : IntegralHom.ReductionPresentation l E X D hl a n)
    (K L : completedIntegralDerivedCategory l E X D hl) :
    integralHomReductionComparison D l hl E X n K L =
      IntegralHom.comparison l E X D hl m K L
